questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Electric flux $\phi$ is related with linear charge density $\lambda$ and surface charge density $\sigma$ as $\phi = \alpha \lambda + \beta \sigma$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are of appropriate dimensions. Dimension of $\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is
questions.solution: $\alpha \lambda \equiv \beta \sigma \Rightarrow \frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \frac{\lambda}{\sigma} = \frac{Q/L}{Q/L^2} \equiv L$ (Displacement)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For given velocity-time ($v - t$) graph, find distance travelled at $0.5\text{ sec}$.
questions.solution:
Acceleration $a = \frac{400 - 200}{2} = 100\text{ m/s}^2$
Distance $S = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = 200 \times 0.5 + \frac{1}{2} \times 100 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 100 + 12.5 = 112.5\text{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The displacement of a particle as function of time is $x(t) = A \sin(t) + B \cos^2(t) + Ct^2 + D$. Find dimension of $\left[\frac{ABC}{D}\right]$.
questions.solution:
$[D] = [L]$
$[C] = [LT^{-2}]$
$[B] = [L]$
$[A] = [L]$
So $\left[\frac{ABC}{D}\right] = \frac{L \cdot L \cdot LT^{-2}}{L} = L^2T^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ratio of electric force to gravitational force between two particles having charges $q_1, q_2$ and masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ respectively is (where symbols have their usual meanings)
questions.solution:
$F_g = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2}$
$F_e = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$
$\frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 G m_1 m_2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Match the column appropriately regarding thermodynamic process.

Column-I:
(P) When volume change is zero
(Q) When pressure is constant
(R) When no heat is exchanged
(S) Work done by the gas is equal to heat given to the gas

Column-II:
(i) $\Delta W = 0$
(ii) $\Delta Q = 0$
(iii) Isobaric
(iv) Isothermal
questions.solution:
Volume change is zero $\rightarrow$ Isochoric $\rightarrow \Delta W = 0$
Isobaric $\Rightarrow \Delta P = 0$
No heat exchange (adiabatic) $\Rightarrow \Delta Q = 0$
Heat given = $\Delta W \Rightarrow \Delta U = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta T = 0$ (Isothermal)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In given DC circuit, find current for $R = 12\ \Omega$ in steady state.
questions.solution:
In steady state, inductor acts as a zero resistance wire / short circuit.
$i = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{12} = 1\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Hot water is less viscous than of cold water.
Statement-II : Surface tension of soap bubble is more than that of a drop of water.
options: Statement-I is true and statement-II true
Statement-I is true and statement-II false
Statement-I is false and statement-II true
Statement-I is false and statement-II false
questions.solution:
Viscosity of liquids decreases with temperature, so hot water is less viscous than cold water (Statement-I is true).
Surface tension of soap solution is less than pure water (Statement-II is false).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The key shown in the circuit is closed at $t = 0$. Choose the incorrect option regarding the conditions at $t = 0$.
options: Current in the circuit is zero
Voltage across the capacitor is minimum
Current in the circuit is maximum
questions.solution: Immediately after closing the key, the capacitor acts as a short circuit i.e., path of zero resistance. Hence, current is maximum at $t = 0$. Thus, 'Current in the circuit is zero' is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform solid sphere of mass $m$ rolls down from rest to achieve speed $v_1$ on an inclined plane of $30^\circ$. Sphere achieves speed $v_2$ on an inclined plane of $45^\circ$ when released from same height then $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}$ is (assume no slipping)
questions.solution:
$|\Delta U| = |\Delta K| \Rightarrow mgh = \frac{1}{2}(\gamma + 1)mv^2$ where $\gamma = \frac{2}{5}$.
Here $v$ doesn't depend on $\theta$, so $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = 1$ for a solid sphere.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Find the equation of magnetic field for the given equation of electric field (for EM wave):
$\vec{E} = E_0 (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$
questions.solution:
Phase difference between magnetic field and electric field is zero.
Magnitude $|\vec{B}| = \frac{E_0 \cdot 5}{C}$.
Direction of wave propagation is $+\hat{k}$, which is along $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.
$(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) \times (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) = 16\hat{k} - (-9\hat{k}) = 25\hat{k}$.
So unit vector along $\vec{B}$ is $\frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{5}$.
Therefore, $\vec{B} = \frac{E_0}{C}(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Self-inductance depends on :
questions.solution: $L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 V$, where $\mu_r$ is relative permeability of medium and $V$ is volume (geometry). Hence, self-inductance depends on geometry and medium property.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
For the circuit shown below:
(A) Current in ammeter is 2 A
(B) Net resistance is $8\ \Omega$
(C) Voltage across BC is 4 V
(D) Current through diode is 1 A
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution:
Diode is forward biased. $R_{eq} = 4 + \frac{4 \times 4}{4 + 4} = 6\ \Omega$.
$i = \frac{12}{6} = 2\text{ A}$ (Ammeter current).
$i_{AB} = 1\text{ A}$ (Current through diode).
$V_{BC} = 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ V}$.
Statements A, C, D are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the time period of a cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10 g oscillating in water. (density of water = $10^3\text{ kg/m}^3$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$a = -\frac{F}{m} = -\frac{\Delta B}{m} = -\frac{(10\text{ cm})^2 x (10^3\text{ kg/m}^3)(10\text{ m/s}^2)}{10\text{ g}} = -10^4 x$
$\omega = 100\text{ rad/s}$
$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{\pi}{50}\text{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Adiabatic constant of a gas is $\frac{3}{2}$. If volume of gas initially at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is reduced to one fourth of the original volume then new temperature is
questions.solution:
$T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$
$273 \cdot V^{1/2} = T \left(\frac{V}{4}\right)^{1/2}$
$T = 2 \times 273 = 546\text{ K}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two objects are equal distances from sphere of radius $R$ & refractive index $\mu$ such that the image of one object forms on other object. Find the object distance from the surface of sphere.
questions.solution:
After first refraction the ray must become parallel to the line joining two objects, so $v = \infty$.
$\frac{\mu_2}{v} - \frac{\mu_1}{u} = \frac{\mu_2 - \mu_1}{R} \Rightarrow 0 - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R} \Rightarrow |u| = \frac{R}{\mu - 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: There is force field $\vec{F} = x^3 y \hat{i} + y^2 \hat{j}$ in which a particle moves along the line $x = y$. Find work done by the force as the particle moves from $(0, 0)$ to $(2, 2)$
questions.solution: $W = \int x^4 dx + \int_0^2 y^2 dy = \left[\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^2 + \left[\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \frac{32}{5} + \frac{8}{3} = \frac{136}{15}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a radioactive decay, decay constant of element $A_2$ is 3 times that of element $A_1$. Find the ratio of nuclei of element 1 to element 2 after one half life of $A_2$ (Assume initial number of nuclei are same for both elements)
questions.solution:
$N_1 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_1 t}$, $N_2 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_2 t}$
$\lambda_2 = 3\lambda_1$, $t = t_{1/2}(A_2) = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda_2} = \frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}$
$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = e^{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)t} = e^{2\lambda_1 \left(\frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}\right)} = e^{\frac{2}{3} \ln 2} = 2^{2/3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: From a uniform circular disc of radius 20 cm a circular portion of radius 5 cm is removed. The shift in the position of centre of mass (in cm) is:
questions.solution: $X_{com} = \frac{M \times 15}{M - \frac{M}{16}} = \frac{15}{15} = 1\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bullet of kinetic energy of 125 J strikes a lead block where temperature rises by $50^\circ\text{C}$. If specific heat of lead is $0.1\text{ J/g-}^\circ\text{C}$ then mass of lead block is (Assume half of kinetic energy of bullet is converted to heat) $m$ gram then $2m$ is:
questions.solution:
$Q = ms\Delta T \Rightarrow \frac{125}{2} = m \times 0.1 \times 50$
$m = 12.5\text{ g}$
$2m = 25$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Which of the following compound can react with Hinsberg reagent?
(A) Aniline
(B) N,N-Dimethyl aniline
(C) Methyl amine
(D) N-phenyl aniline
questions.solution: Primary ($1^\circ$) and secondary ($2^\circ$) amines react with Hinsberg reagent. Aniline ($1^\circ$), Methyl amine ($1^\circ$), and N-phenyl aniline ($2^\circ$) react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among the following, the most stable carbanion is
questions.solution: Cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic ($6\pi$ electrons) and hence most stable.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following compound can show fac-mer isomerism?
questions.solution: $[\text{Ma}_3\text{b}_3]$ type complex compounds can show facial-meridional (fac-mer) isomerism, where $a$ and $b$ are monodentate ligands.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following pair of ions have same colour?
questions.solution: Both $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ are blue in aqueous solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following does not belong to the same period in the modern periodic table?
questions.solution: Os, Ir, Pt belong to the $6^{\text{th}}$ period, while Pd belongs to the $5^{\text{th}}$ period of the modern periodic table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Identify the product formed in the following reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO} + \text{HCHO (Excess)} \xrightarrow[\text{Reflux}]{\text{OH}^-}$$
questions.solution: Propanal undergoes aldol condensation with excess HCHO to form 2,2-dihydroxymethylpropanal, which further undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with HCHO to give 2,2-dihydroxymethylpropan-1-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Incorrect statement among the following is
options: $\text{SO}_2$ act as oxidising agent but not reducing agent
questions.solution: $\text{SO}_2$ acts as both an oxidising and reducing agent as sulphur is in the +4 oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions and find the molecular mass of the final product (A) formed in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$:
$$\text{p-nitrotoluene} \xrightarrow{(i)\ \text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3,\ (ii)\ \text{Sn}/\text{HCl}} \xrightarrow{(iii)\ \text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}\ (0-5^\circ\text{C})} \xrightarrow{(iv)\ \text{H}_3\text{PO}_2} (A)$$
questions.solution: (A) is 3-bromotoluene ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{Br}$). Molecular mass = $7 \times 12 + 7 \times 1 + 80 = 171\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the Column I with Column II and choose the correct option.

Column I:
A. $\text{BF}_3$
B. $\text{CCl}_4, \text{CO}_2$
C. $\text{PCl}_5, \text{BrF}_5$
D. $\text{NO}$

Column II:
(i) Odd $\text{e}^-$ species
(ii) Expanded octet
(iii) Complete octet
(iv) Electron deficient
questions.solution:
$\text{BF}_3$: $6\text{e}^-$ (Electron deficient)
$\text{CCl}_4, \text{CO}_2$: $8\text{e}^-$ (Complete octet)
$\text{PCl}_5, \text{BrF}_5$: $>8\text{e}^-$ (Expanded octet)
$\text{NO}$: Odd electron species

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the column and choose the correct option:

Column-I:
(A) $2\text{Ph}-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/D.E.}}$
(B) $\text{Ph}-\text{N}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{CuCl/HCl}}$
(C) $\text{Ph}-\text{Cl} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/D.E.}}$
(D) $\text{CH}_3-\text{Cl} + \text{AgF} \rightarrow$

(Q) Fittig reaction
(R) Wurtz-Fittig reaction

questions.solution:
A $\rightarrow$ Fittig reaction (Q)
B $\rightarrow$ Sandmeyer reaction (P)
C $\rightarrow$ Wurtz-Fittig reaction (R)
D $\rightarrow$ Swarts reaction (S)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is forming an octahedral complex with spin only magnetic moment 3.83 BM. The correct electronic configuration for cobalt in the complex is?
questions.solution:
$\mu = 3.83\text{ BM} \Rightarrow n = 3$ unpaired electrons.
$\text{Co}^{2+} = 3d^7$. For weak field ligand, configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : During Lassaigne’s test, covalent compound is converted to ionic compound.
Statement-II : $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ gives Prussian blue colour on reaction with $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$.
options: S-I is correct, S-II is incorrect
S-I is incorrect, S-II is correct
Both S-I and S-II are correct
Both S-I and S-II are incorrect
questions.solution: Both statements S-I and S-II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the reaction $A(g) \rightarrow 2B(g)$, initial pressure was $0.6\text{ atm}$ and rate constant is $4.606 \times 10^{-2}\text{ sec}^{-1}$. Find the total pressure at $100\text{ sec}$.
questions.solution:
$kt = 2.303 \log \frac{P_0}{P_0 - p} \Rightarrow 4.606 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 = 2.303 \log \frac{0.6}{0.6 - p}$
$\log \frac{0.6}{0.6 - p} = 2 \Rightarrow p = 0.594\text{ atm}$
Total pressure $= 0.6 + p = 0.6 + 0.594 = 1.194\text{ atm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
Statement-I: Fructose does not contain aldehyde group but it gives Tollen's test.
Statement-II: In disaccharides, if the reducing groups are bonded, these are non-reducing sugar e.g., sucrose. If these functional groups are free then they are reducing sugar e.g. maltose and Lactose.
options: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, Statement-II is correct
Statement-I and Statement-II both are incorrect
questions.solution:
Fructose tautomerises to aldehyde in basic medium and reduces Tollen's reagent (Statement-I is correct).
In sucrose, reducing groups are bonded (non-reducing), while in maltose and lactose they are free (reducing) (Statement-II is correct).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For a sample of Hydrogen atom, the wavelength observed is $656\text{ nm}$ during a transition. The transition and corresponding series in hydrogen spectrum will be
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$
For Balmer series $n_1 = 2$, $3 \rightarrow 2$ gives $\lambda = 656\text{ nm}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: If 2 g phenol is allowed to react with $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. How much $\text{Br}_2$ (in g) will be required to produce 2, 4, 6 tribromophenol (Rounded off to nearest integer).
questions.solution:
3 moles of $\text{Br}_2$ react with 1 mole of phenol.
$\text{Br}_2$ required $= \frac{2}{94} \times 160 \times 3 = 10.2\text{ g} \approx 10\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: When $10^{21}$ molecules are removed from $x\text{ mg}$ of $\text{CO}_2(g)$, then $2.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ moles}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ are left. Calculate the value of $x$. [Take $N_A = 6 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Moles removed $= \frac{10^{21}}{6 \times 10^{23}} = 1.67 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$
Total moles $= 2.4 \times 10^{-3} + 1.67 \times 10^{-3} = 4.07 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$
Mass $= 4.07 \times 10^{-3} \times 44 = 179 \times 10^{-3}\text{ g} = 179\text{ mg}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following Latimer diagram:
$$\text{FeO}_4^{2-} \xrightarrow{2.0\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{3+} \xrightarrow{0.8\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{2+} \xrightarrow{-0.5\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^0$$
Find $E^0_{\text{FeO}_4^{2-}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}$ (in V, rounded off to nearest integer).
questions.solution:
$-4 \times F \times E^0 = -3 \times F \times 2 + (-1 \times F \times 0.8)$
$-4E^0 = -6.8 \Rightarrow E^0 = 1.7\text{ V} \approx 2\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the given values:
$\Delta H = 55\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta S = 175\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$
$T = 25^\circ\text{C}$
Calculate the value of Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G$) in $\text{J mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = 55000 - 298 \times 175 = 55000 - 52150 = 2850\text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In estimation of sulphur by Carius method, 160 g of organic compound gives 466 g of Barium sulphate. % of sulphur in the organic compound is _____.
questions.solution:
233 g $\text{BaSO}_4$ contains 32 g sulphur.
466 g $\text{BaSO}_4$ contains 64 g sulphur.
$\% \text{ sulphur} = \frac{64}{160} \times 100 = 40\%$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: How many words can be formed from the word “DAUGHTER” such that any vowels are not together
questions.solution: Total arrangements - Vowels together $= 8! - 6! \times 3! = 40320 - 720 \times 6 = 36000$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two biased dies are tossed. Die 1 has 1 on two faces, 2 on two faces, 3 and 4 on other faces, while die 2 has 2 on 2 faces, 4 on 2 faces and 1 and 3 on other faces. Then the probability that when throwing these dices we get sum of 4 or 5.
questions.solution:
$P(\text{sum} = 4) = \left(\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{2}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{1}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{6} \times \frac{1}{6}\right) = \frac{7}{36}$
$P(\text{sum} = 5) = \left(\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{2}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{1}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{6} \times \frac{2}{6}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{6} \times \frac{1}{6}\right) = \frac{9}{36}$
$P = \frac{7}{36} + \frac{9}{36} = \frac{16}{36} = \frac{4}{9}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Value of $\cos^{-1}\left[\frac{12}{13}\cos x + \frac{5}{13}\sin x\right]$ for $x \in \left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\tan \alpha = \frac{5}{12} \Rightarrow \sin \alpha = \frac{5}{13}, \cos \alpha = \frac{12}{13}$.
Expression $= \cos^{-1}[\cos(x - \alpha)] = x - \alpha = x - \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation defined on set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, then how many ordered pairs are added to $R = \{(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3)\}$ so that it becomes equivalence relation?
questions.solution:
Ordered pairs to be added: $\{(1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 4), (2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1), (1, 3)\}$.
Total 7 ordered pairs.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of all rational terms in the expansion of $\left(1 + 2^{1/3} + 3^{1/2}\right)^6$ is
questions.solution:
General term: $\frac{6!}{\alpha! \beta! \gamma!} (1)^\alpha (2^{1/3})^\beta (3^{1/2})^\gamma$.
For rational terms, $3 \mid \beta$ and $2 \mid \gamma$.
Cases $(\beta, \gamma, \alpha)$:
$(0,0,6) \rightarrow 27$
$(0,2,4) \rightarrow 45$
$(0,4,2) \rightarrow 135$
$(0,6,0) \rightarrow 27$
$(3,0,3) \rightarrow 40$
$(3,2,1) \rightarrow 360$
$(6,0,0) \rightarrow 4$
Sum $= 27 + 45 + 135 + 27 + 40 + 360 + 4 = 638$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\left|\frac{z}{z + i}\right| = 2$ represents a circle with centre $P$ then distance of $P$ from $D(1, 5)$ is
questions.solution:
$|z| = 2|z + i| \Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 = 4(x^2 + (y + 1)^2) \Rightarrow 3x^2 + 3y^2 + 8y + 4 = 0$.
Centre $P = \left(0, -\frac{4}{3}\right)$.
Distance $PD = \sqrt{(1 - 0)^2 + \left(5 + \frac{4}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 + \frac{361}{9}} = \sqrt{\frac{370}{9}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider the set $S = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, 1000\}$. Then the number of arithmetic progression that can be formed using elements of set $S$ such that first term is 1 and last term is 1000 is
questions.solution:
$T_n = a + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow 1000 = 1 + (n - 1)d \Rightarrow (n - 1)d = 999 = 37 \times 27 = 37^1 \times 3^3$.
Number of divisors of $999 = (1 + 1)(3 + 1) = 8$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $f(x) = \log_e x$ and $g(x) = \frac{2x^4 - 2x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 1}{2x^2 - 2x + 1}$, then domain of $f(g(x))$ for $x > 0$ is
questions.solution:
$g(x) = \frac{(2x^2 - 2x + 1)(x^2 - 1)}{2x^2 - 2x + 1} = x^2 - 1$.
$f(g(x)) = \log_e (x^2 - 1) > 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow x \in (1, \infty)$ for $x > 0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the curve satisfying the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{6 - 2e^{2x}y}{1 + e^{2x}} = 0$ passes through $(0, 0)$ and $(\ln 2, k)$, then $k$ is
questions.solution:
$\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(\frac{2e^{2x}}{1 + e^{2x}}\right)y = \frac{6}{1 + e^{2x}}$
$\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \frac{2e^{2x}}{1 + e^{2x}} dx} = 1 + e^{2x}$
$y(1 + e^{2x}) = \int 6 dx = 6x + c$
Passes through $(0, 0) \Rightarrow c = 0 \Rightarrow y = \frac{6x}{1 + e^{2x}}$
For $x = \ln 2$: $k = \frac{6\ln 2}{1 + 4} = \frac{6}{5}\ln 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, where
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{2}{x}(\sin(k_1 + 1)x + \sin(k_2 + 1)x), & x < 0 \\ 4, & x = 0 \\ \frac{2}{x}\log\left[\frac{k_2 x + 1}{k_1 x + 1}\right], & x > 0 \end{cases}$$
Then $k_1^2 + k_2^2$ is
questions.solution:
LHL at $x = 0$: $2(k_1 + 1 + k_2 + 1) = 4 \Rightarrow k_1 + k_2 = 0$.
RHL at $x = 0$: $2(k_2 - k_1) = 4 \Rightarrow k_2 - k_1 = 2$.
Solving gives $k_1 = -1, k_2 = 1$.
$k_1^2 + k_2^2 = 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
If for the system of linear equations having infinite solutions
$(\lambda - 4)x + (\lambda - 2)y + \lambda z = 0$
$2x + 3y + 5z = 0$
$x + 2y + 6z = 0$
then $\lambda^2 + \lambda$ is
questions.solution:
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} \lambda - 4 & \lambda - 2 & \lambda \\ 2 & 3 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 0 \Rightarrow 2\lambda - 18 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 9$.
$\lambda^2 + \lambda = 81 + 9 = 90$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the equation $a(b - c)x^2 + b(c - a)x + c(a - b) = 0$ has equal roots and if $a + c = 5$ and $b = \frac{16}{5}$, then the value of $a^2 + c^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$x = 1$ is a root. Since roots are equal, both roots are 1.
Product of roots $= \frac{c(a - b)}{a(b - c)} = 1 \Rightarrow 2ac = b(a + c) = \frac{16}{5} \times 5 = 16$.
$a^2 + c^2 = (a + c)^2 - 2ac = 25 - 16 = 9$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The area of larger portion enclosed by curves $y = |x - 1|$ and $x^2 + y^2 = 25$ is equal to $\frac{1}{4}(\alpha\pi + \beta)$ sq. units (where $\alpha, \beta$ are natural numbers), then $\alpha + \beta$ equals to
questions.solution:
$A = 25\pi - \int_{-3}^4 (\sqrt{25 - x^2} - |x - 1|) dx = \frac{1}{4}(75\pi + 2)$.
$\alpha = 75, \beta = 2 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 77$.
